seo.title: Homeless help in Los Angeles - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Los Angeles: shelter, meals, health care, jobs, ID, benefits, and legal help.

page.heading: Los Angeles homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, police, fire, or ambulance: 911 Adult or youth shelter line: 800-548-6047 Families, food, benefits, and local services: 211 County mental health and substance-use help: 800-854-7771, 24 hours
page.notice: Beds, schedules, routes, and eligibility can change. Call before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, money, or job the same day. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.
page.intro:
When asking for help, give your exact location or nearest landmark, whether you have a safe place tonight, when you last ate, medical needs, age, pregnancy or disability, children or pets with you, and whether you have identification. Ask the worker to explain the next step, required documents, transportation, and what to do if no bed is open.
Best first call: adults and young people seeking a bed can call 800-548-6047; households with a child under 18 should call 211. A Coordinated Entry access center can also assess housing needs. Shelter placement is based on eligibility and availability.
page.footer: Is something wrong or outdated? Submit a correction. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for: immediate violence, serious injury, trouble breathing, loss of consciousness, fire, overdose, or another life-threatening emergency. Give a precise location and describe the danger first.
City of Los Angeles homeless-services guidance

entries.title: LAHSA shelter line
entries.description:
Phone: 800-548-6047.
Use it for: adult shelter and shelter for youth ages 16–24. Tell the operator your age, household, location, health or mobility needs, pets, and whether you need transportation.
LAHSA Coordinated Entry — get help

entries.title: 211 LA
entries.description:
Phone: 211, 24 hours.
Use it for: family shelter, food, benefits, health, legal, domestic-violence, and other local referrals. Ask the operator to check current eligibility and hours rather than relying on an old address.
City crisis-response resource list

entries.title: County behavioral-health help line
entries.description:
Phone: 800-854-7771, free and available 24 hours.
Service: mental-health and substance-use referrals, crisis assessment, field response, interpretation, and transportation when appropriate. Call 911 if there is immediate physical danger.
LA County Department of Mental Health — get help now

entries.title: Coordinated Entry System
entries.description:
Adults and youth: 800-548-6047; families with a child: 211.
Service: assessment and connection to emergency, interim, and permanent-housing programs. An assessment is not a promise of immediate housing; keep your contact details current with the caseworker.
LAHSA Coordinated Entry System

entries.title: Union Rescue Mission — emergency shelter
entries.description:
Weekday intake: 213-347-6351, Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; after hours: 213-316-2711.
Who: single adults and several family types. The published intake requires proof of ID and a Megan's Law clearance; call first if you lack ID.
Union Rescue Mission — current intake
entries.address: Address: 545 S. San Pedro Street, Los Angeles, CA 90013

entries.title: Los Angeles Mission
entries.description:
Main phone: 213-629-1227; men's intake extension 309, women's intake extension 518.
Service: emergency services, recovery-oriented residential programs, meals, showers, clothing, classes, and employment help. Call for current bed and intake rules.
Los Angeles Mission — need help
entries.address: Address: 303 E. 5th Street, Los Angeles, CA 90013

entries.title: The Midnight Mission
entries.description:
Phone: 213-624-9258 or 888-624-9258.
Service: shelter and supportive services for single men and women, emergency food, personal goods, housing help, and recovery programs. Confirm current intake before arrival.
LA County service listing
entries.address: Address: 601 S. San Pedro Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

entries.title: Emmanuel Baptist Rescue Mission — nightly beds for men
entries.description:
Bed sign-up: 6:30 p.m., first come, first served; the door sign states that night's available beds.
Service: a brief Christian service, dinner, shower, bed, and breakfast. Because capacity is limited, also call the LAHSA shelter line rather than relying on one location.
Emmanuel Baptist Rescue Mission

entries.title: Covenant House California — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 323-461-3131; emergency services are open 24 hours and walk-ins are accepted.
Service: free emergency shelter, meals, showers, clothing, health care, education, employment, transportation, and case management for young adults, including LGBTQ+ youth.
Covenant House Los Angeles
entries.address: Address: 1325 N. Western Avenue, Los Angeles, CA 90027

entries.title: Safe Parking
entries.description:
Referral: use the LAHSA safe-parking list or call 211.
Service: legal overnight parking for people living in a vehicle; city-listed sites have restrooms and security. Registration, vehicle documents, hours, and rules vary by lot.
City of Los Angeles — Safe Parking programs

entries.title: Domestic-violence shelter placement
entries.description:
County hotline: 800-978-3600, confidential and open 24 hours.
Service: safety planning and connection to confidential emergency shelter and longer-term housing for survivors and children. Call 911 if the danger is immediate.
City domestic-violence resources

entries.title: Los Angeles Mission — community meals
entries.description:
Published meal times: breakfast 5:30 a.m., lunch 12:30 p.m., and dinner 6:45 p.m. Meals, showers, and clothing are among the emergency services; confirm the daily line and any changes.
Los Angeles Mission meal and service information

entries.title: Union Rescue Mission — meals and hygiene
entries.description:
Phone: 213-347-6351.
Service: three meals daily for guests, showers, haircuts, clothing, and laundry. Community access and intake rules can differ from resident services, so call first.
Union Rescue Mission emergency services

entries.title: The Midnight Mission — meals and restrooms
entries.description:
Phone: 213-624-9258. The organization provides emergency food and personal goods; a current county listing confirms weekday service. Call for today's meal and shower times.
LA County resource listing

entries.title: Hospitality Kitchen — Los Angeles Catholic Worker
entries.description:
Phone: 213-614-9615.
Published service: food Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, 7:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m. Confirm the current schedule before making a long trip.
Skid Row service resource list
entries.address: Address: 821 E. 6th Street, Los Angeles, CA 90021

entries.title: Bee a Little Better — Thursday meal
entries.description:
Published time: Thursday around 6:30 p.m.
Service: hot meals, water, toiletries, first-aid supplies, and donated seasonal items. Outdoor distribution can be canceled or moved, so check the organization first.
Bee a Little Better
entries.address: Location: Union Church parking lot, 401 E. 3rd Street

entries.title: 211 food-resource search
entries.description:
Phone: 211.
Service: current referrals to food pantries and meal programs across Los Angeles County. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and ask whether ID, proof of address, or an appointment is required.
LAHSA — food-resource referral

entries.title: Union Rescue Mission
entries.description:
Main phone: 213-347-6300.
Support: Christian mission offering shelter, meals, hygiene, medical, dental, legal, mental-health, recovery, and family services. Some programs require ID and screening.
Union Rescue Mission

entries.title: Los Angeles Mission
entries.description:
Phone: 213-629-1227.
Support: meals, showers, clothing, recovery, education, employment workshops, job-search help, psychiatric referrals, and a free legal clinic.
Los Angeles Mission services

entries.title: The Midnight Mission
entries.description:
Phone: 213-624-9258.
Support: secular homeless services including shelter, food, housing help, personal goods, recovery, and education. Ask intake which services are available without a shelter placement.
LA County listing

entries.title: Los Angeles Public Library homeless resources
entries.description:
Service: local libraries can connect people to jobs, food, housing, computers, and other support. Ask 311 or the library system for the closest branch and current social-service schedule.
City homeless-services page — library resources

entries.title: Medical emergency — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for: overdose, unconsciousness, serious injury, severe breathing trouble, chest pain, heavy bleeding, or another life-threatening condition. Do not delay because of insurance or ID concerns.
LA County urgent-help guidance

entries.title: JWCH Center for Community Health
entries.description:
Appointments: 866-733-5924.
Service: community health clinic serving people in and around Skid Row, including medical outreach and HIV and STI testing and treatment. Call for current hours, cost, and walk-in rules.
LA County health locator
entries.address: Address: 522 S. San Pedro Street, Los Angeles, CA 90013

entries.title: LA County behavioral-health help line
entries.description:
Phone: 800-854-7771, 24 hours.
Service: mental-health and substance-use support, screening, referrals, crisis assessment, field response, interpretation, and transport. Ask specifically for homeless outreach if needed.
ACCESS Center

entries.title: Substance Abuse Service Helpline
entries.description:
Phone: 844-804-7500.
Service: information and connection to substance-use treatment in Los Angeles County. Tell the operator if you have no phone, transportation, insurance, or safe place to stay.
LA County crisis and service lines

entries.title: Shelter-based medical and dental referrals
entries.description:
Union Rescue Mission: 213-347-6351; Los Angeles Mission: 213-629-1227.
Service: URM publishes medical, dental, legal, and mental-health care for guests; LA Mission offers psychiatric referrals. Ask what is available to a person not yet admitted.
URM emergency services

entries.title: 211 LA — benefits and social-service navigation
entries.description:
Phone: 211.
Service: referrals for food, shelter, health, financial support, legal help, and county programs. Ask for the correct benefits office and the documents needed for CalFresh or other aid.
City resource list — 211 LA

entries.title: LA-HOP homeless outreach request
entries.description:
Use: request non-emergency outreach for a person living outside. Provide a precise, publicly accessible location and useful description. Do not use it for immediate danger; call 911 instead.
LAPD homeless-services FAQ and LA-HOP guidance

entries.title: City services — 311
entries.description:
Phone: 311.
Service: city information and non-emergency service requests. For shelter placement call 800-548-6047 or 211; for outreach, ask for LA-HOP.
Official Los Angeles homelessness FAQ

entries.title: Housing help through a county clinic
entries.description:
Health Services patient line: 844-804-0055.
Service: county Health Services can connect patients to clinics and housing resources, including Coordinated Entry, shelter, safe parking, domestic-violence shelter, and eviction prevention.
LA County Health Services — housing resources

entries.title: WorkSource Centers
entries.description:
Service: the City network provides job-readiness workshops, training, job search, and employer connections, including services for people experiencing homelessness.
Next step: use the official center list or ask 311 for the nearest active WorkSource Center; confirm ID and appointment requirements.
City WorkSource network information

entries.title: Los Angeles Mission employment help
entries.description:
Phone: 213-629-1227.
Service: employment-readiness workshops, job-search assistance, GED preparation, computer skills, ESL, vocational training, and referrals. Intake depends on the service or residential program.
Los Angeles Mission programs

entries.title: Covenant House — work and education for ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 323-461-3131.
Service: education enrollment, tutoring, GED, ESL, employment services, case management, and transportation for young adults in its programs.
Covenant House Los Angeles

entries.title: Legal barriers to employment
entries.description:
NLSLA: 800-433-6251.
Service: free help for eligible people with license reinstatement, unpaid tickets, unemployment benefits, credit, and criminal-record clearing. A shelter or housing worker can also send a referral.
Neighborhood Legal Services — homelessness

entries.title: Neighborhood Legal Services Los Angeles
entries.description:
Phone: 800-433-6251.
Service: free help for eligible people experiencing or nearing homelessness with housing, benefits, family law, restraining orders, tickets, license reinstatement, credit, and record clearing.
NLSLA homeless legal services

entries.title: Community Outreach Court
entries.description:
Service: helps people experiencing homelessness resolve eligible bench warrants, misdemeanor cases, citations, fines, fees, and convictions, and connects participants to housing and job support.
LA County Public Defender — Community Outreach Courts
entries.how_to_access: Access: ask a homeless-services caseworker for a current referral and court location; eligibility differs by case.

entries.title: Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles
entries.description:
Phone: 800-399-4529.
Service: free help for eligible low-income residents with housing, benefits, immigration, family, and record-clearing matters. Representation depends on the case and capacity.
City 2026 legal-referral bulletin
entries.address: Office: 1550 W. 8th Street, Los Angeles, CA 90017

entries.title: Eviction Defense Network
entries.description:
Phone: 213-385-8112.
Service: pre-eviction, eviction, notices to vacate, court preparation, and housing advice. The 2026 city bulletin lists weekday walk-in, first-come service; confirm before visiting.
Los Angeles Housing Department legal referrals
entries.address: Address: 207 S. Broadway, 6th floor, Los Angeles, CA 90012

entries.title: California no-fee ID card
entries.description:
How: ask a government agency or qualifying nonprofit serving unhoused people to verify your status and issue the DMV verification form before visiting DMV.
California DMV — identification cards
entries.how_to_access: Eligibility: a person meeting the federal definition of homelessness may qualify for a no-fee California identification card.

entries.title: DMV verification and address letters
entries.description:
Documents: a qualified provider issues the no-fee verification. For a REAL ID, an applicant may use the verification plus a letter from a shelter, nonprofit, faith organization, employer, or government agency attesting California residence.
Ask first: a Coordinated Entry caseworker, mission, or public-benefits office whether it is registered to issue the form.
DMV no-fee ID program rules

entries.title: ID help through a shelter or caseworker
entries.description:
Start with: the shelter line at 800-548-6047 or 211.
Ask for: identity-document replacement, a mailing address, fee-verification form, and help obtaining birth records. Keep copies and receipts separate from original documents.
LAHSA Coordinated Entry

entries.title: LA County domestic-violence hotline
entries.description:
Phone: 800-978-3600, confidential and open 24 hours.
Service: safety planning, emergency-shelter referrals, counseling, housing, and legal resources for survivors and children. Use a safe phone when possible; call 911 for immediate danger.
City domestic-violence resources

entries.title: Women and Children's Crisis Shelter
entries.description:
24-hour line: 562-945-3939.
Service: English and Spanish crisis support, safety planning, referrals, and information about intake availability for a 45-day emergency shelter. Other languages can be arranged.
Emergency Lifeline

entries.title: Covenant House — young adults
entries.description:
Phone: 323-461-3131, 24 hours.
Who: ages 18–24, including young people at risk of trafficking and LGBTQ+ youth. Walk-in emergency shelter and services are free.
Covenant House California

entries.title: Child abuse and neglect hotline
entries.description:
Phone: 800-540-4000; TTY 800-272-6699.
Use it for: suspected abuse or neglect of a child in Los Angeles County. Call 911 if a child is in immediate danger or needs emergency medical care.
LA County crisis hotlines

entries.title: Human trafficking help
entries.description:
Phone: 888-373-7888; text: 233733.
Use it for: forced labor, commercial sexual exploitation, withheld ID, threats, or inability to leave. Do not confront a suspected exploiter; call 911 if danger is immediate.
LA County human-trafficking resource
